findings.passage: Summary: This proposition is my favorite, because I had the honor of carrying and passing it in the Texas House.
findings.note: From her official House newsletter (written before the 2025-11-04 vote), on Proposition 16, SJR 37, 'Requiring US Citizenship to Vote.'

findings.passage: Passing this amendment will make it clear that non-citizens are disqualified from voting in any election in Texas.
findings.note: From her official House newsletter, explaining Proposition 16 (SJR 37) to voters.

findings.passage: In the most recent session, Candy was House author of the bill to restore the Ten Commandments to public school classrooms and House author of the bill ensuring that only U.S. citizens can vote in Texas elections.
findings.note: From her campaign site (page undated; it says the amendment was approved by voters, so it was written after November 2025). The page lists 'Improving Border Security, Texas Security, Election Integrity' as a heading.

findings.passage: Sponsored a constitutional amendment, approved overwhelmingly by Texas voters, ensuring that only U.S. citizens can vote in Texas elections
findings.note: Bullet on her campaign site (page undated; written after November 2025) about the citizenship-to-vote amendment.

findings.motion: Author of HJR 161, constitutional amendment on citizenship to vote
findings.note: Official bill page shows her as author of HJR 161 (89th Legislature, 2025). Last action shown: laid on the table subject to call, 2025-05-09. Its Senate version SJR 37 went to the ballot.

findings.motion: House sponsor of SJR 37, constitutional amendment on citizenship to vote
findings.note: SJR 37 (89th Legislature, 2025) is titled 'Proposing a constitutional amendment clarifying that a voter must be a United States citizen.' Official bill page lists her as House sponsor. The page's action list shows House third reading on 2025-05-10 and adoption on 2025-05-12.
